title: Closed structure ideal product, normalized by its inclusion
statement: Let $i:W\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Its extended ideal $I\mathcal O_W$ is $I.\mathrm{comap}(i)$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. There is an isomorphism $e:i_*(I\mathcal O_W)\xrightarrow{\sim}I(i_*\mathcal O_W)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk] such that the composite of $e$ with the product inclusion into $i_*\mathcal O_W$ equals the pushforward of the ideal inclusion $I\mathcal O_W\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_W$. No Noetherianity or integrality is required.

source.place: Tag 01QY (lemma-closed-immersion-pushforward), affine quotient calculation; also the affine ideal-product comparison in the proof of Tag 088A.

proof.text: Use the existing qcqs quasi-coherent pushforward theorem and quasi-coherent kernel theorem directly to obtain the ideal-module and structure-pushforward instances. On any open the image/abelian-image isomorphism identifies their section ranges. On affine opens the existing image-section and tensor-section theorems show that the image of any morphism from a quasi-coherent tensor product to a quasi-coherent module is generated by the images of pure tensor sections. Specialize this general calculation to ideal multiplication using the unitor section formula.

For an affine V, its preimage U is affine and pi=i.app V is surjective. The comap ideal formula gives J(U)=Ideal.map pi I(V). A right unitor and the image strong-epi/mono isomorphism identify J times O_W with J, preserving inclusions. Compare pure products: every element of the mapped ideal lifts to an element of I(V), and conversely every element of I(V) maps into J(U). Restricted scalar multiplication identifies the products. Hence both inclusions have equal ranges on V.

Prove the affine-section criterion for equality of any two module morphisms using sheaf separatedness. Prove the equivalence between subobject order and affine section-range inclusion: order gives a factorization via Subobject.ofMkLEMk; in the reverse direction the composite with the other inclusion's cokernel vanishes by affine equality, and its kernel lift factors through the monic image. Apply both directions of the range equality to obtain subobject equality, and use Subobject.isoOfMkEqMk for the inclusion-compatible isomorphism.

theorem closed_structure_ideal_product_iso
    {X W : Scheme.{u}} (i : W ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    ∃ e : (pushforward i).obj (I.comap i).toModules ≅
        idealModuleProduct I.toModulesι
          ((pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit W.ringCatSheaf)),
      e.hom ≫ idealModuleProductι I.toModulesι
          ((pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit W.ringCatSheaf)) =
        (pushforward i).map (I.comap i).toModulesι
